title: Asynchronous Background Job Processing & Dead-Letter Queues
learningObjectives: Decouple heavy processing from HTTP request cycles using reliable message brokers
Design idempotent job workers that survive ungraceful process crashes
Configure Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) and alerting for unrecoverable poisonous messages
keyTradeoffs: Redis-based lightweight queues (BullMQ) vs distributed persistent logs (RabbitMQ, SQS, Kafka)
At-least-once processing guarantees vs at-most-once performance
commonPitfalls: Passing large payload objects in job metadata instead of entity IDs
Lacking dead-letter queue limits, allowing malformed poison pill jobs to loop endlessly
transferPrompt: How do you coordinate recurring scheduled batch jobs using queue workers without duplicate task execution?
